The graph of the function $y=g(x)$ is shown above. 
Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=6$ using a forward difference approximation with step size $h=4.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x)}{h}
$$

 
at the point $x=6.$  Applying the above formula with $x=6$ and $h=4$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(6) & ≈\frac{g(6+4)-g(6)}{4} \\  & =\frac{g(10)-g(6)}{4} \\  & =\frac{8-2}{4} \\  & =\frac{6}{4} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$
